finding: The supervisor revalidates typed FREE admission and terminates an unadmitted external swarm, but previously inherited or previously admitted provider credential environment values survive a later admission revocation. New local-model, distillery, forge or other child processes can therefore inherit stale provider secrets even though canonical provider I/O wrappers are fail-closed. This is a least-privilege and revocation-boundary gap, not evidence that a new provider request actually occurred.
counterhypothesis: Final provider I/O revalidation is sufficient because stale environment credentials cannot cross the guarded request boundary. This remains an important primary network fence, but it does not justify retaining revoked credentials in the supervisor process or propagating them into newly spawned children. The repair therefore removes revoked secret values at the process boundary while preserving the final provider-I/O admission check.
